_meta.purpose: Single source of commercial truth for the Atomic Shelf website relaunch (PRD Section 32 / Step 1).
sourced_from: https://github.com/Booktok-max/Milky (pricing.html, in-repo build — currently only 4 of the 6 live plans; superseded here by live site data)
_meta.rounding_rule: Discounted long-term commitment totals are rounded DOWN to the nearest $10 (e.g. $97 -> $90). Undiscounted list-price totals (monthly x term) are left exact.
_meta.note_on_source_discrepancy: The Milky repo's pricing.html only contains 4 plans (Spark, Foundation, Momentum, Growth) and no working payment backend URL. The live site has 6 plans (adds Enhanced and Starter). This file uses the live site as current truth per PRD Section 46.
_meta.note_on_enhanced_starter_commitments: The live site does not render a 'See commitment savings' flip-card for Enhanced or Starter, but per your instruction the same 10%/20%/25% (3/6/12-month) discount schedule used on Spark and Foundation applies to them too. Flag for whoever builds the pricing page: this UI needs to be added for these two plans, since right now nothing on-site tells a visitor these discounts exist.
_meta.note_on_audience_positioning_outcome: Resolved 2026-09-22, per your instruction: the earlier draft of these fields invented specific unverified numbers (category-rank ranges, review-count multipliers, download volumes) and was flagged '[extrapolated] / needs sign-off'. Replaced with general, defensible audience/positioning/outcome copy that makes no specific numeric claims. Detailed, client-verified audience and outcome data is still pending and is out of scope for the current build — swap it in here when available; nothing on the site should be rewritten to depend on it in the meantime.
_meta.note_on_momentum_growth_3_month: Resolved 2026-09-22, per your instruction: Momentum and Growth previously only offered 6- and 12-month commitments. Added a 3-month tier to both so all six plans offer uniform commitment options, using the same 10%-off / round-down-to-nearest-$10 rule already applied everywhere else (Momentum: $747 list -> $670; Growth: $1,497 list -> $1,340). These figures were previously only a hardcoded JS literal inside design-system.html's pricing-card demo; this is now the actual source-of-truth record they should have referenced. design-system.html's demo numbers are unchanged and already match. Separately, on 2026-09-22 a math-audit pass found Foundation's 3-month figures ($213 -> $192) were a stale double-discount inherited from the old site copy (10% applied twice to $237 instead of once); corrected to $237 -> $213 -> $210 (rounded) here, consistent with this same rule.

plans.name: Spark
plans.audience: Authors who want to start building a consistent short-form video presence for a specific book, without yet committing to a full marketing campaign.
plans.positioning: The entry point into the system — establishes a steady content cadence and click-through data before you commit to a larger plan.
plans.outcome: A running library of short-form video and click-through data you can use to decide whether to scale up.
services: Genre-matched scripts, viral hooks & trending audio
deliverables: [extrapolated] No listing, review, or retargeting work included at this tier

plans.name: Enhanced
plans.audience: Authors already running Spark-level content who want one reusable flagship asset for ads, a bio link, a newsletter, or reviewer outreach.
plans.positioning: Adds a durable creative asset on top of ongoing content, without moving into full campaign management.
plans.outcome: A cinematic trailer and a richer creative library you can reuse across future campaigns.
deliverables: [extrapolated] Everything in Spark, plus one cinematic trailer
[extrapolated] One long-form video with avatar narration

plans.name: Foundation
plans.audience: Authors with a published book and a live Amazon listing that hasn't been professionally optimized, with no reader list of their own yet.
plans.positioning: The first tier where the listing itself is built to convert the traffic your content sends — and where reader-list building with ShelfMates/StoryPals begins.
plans.outcome: An optimized listing, a configured preorder page, and the start of an owned reader list, alongside ongoing video content.
deliverables: [extrapolated] Rewritten listing copy, keywords, and A+ content

plans.name: Starter
plans.audience: Authors with an optimized (or optimizable) listing who want to add paid amplification for the first time, without managing ad campaigns themselves.
plans.positioning: Layers a managed Amazon DSP budget and additional creative assets on top of Spark-level content — a bridge toward full campaign management.
plans.outcome: Paid reach on top of organic content, plus two trailers and an original theme song, with ad spend managed on your behalf.
deliverables: [extrapolated] $50/month Amazon DSP ad spend managed on the author's behalf

plans.name: Momentum
plans.audience: Authors with an upcoming launch or relaunch, ready for a structured, multi-week preorder push.
plans.positioning: The first full-funnel tier — content, social proof, a scheduled preorder campaign, and retargeting run as one coordinated system.
plans.outcome: A managed launch campaign that combines content, ARC reviews, listing work, and retargeting around a defined preorder countdown.
services: Segmented retargeting, up to 5x daily for 30 days
deliverables: [extrapolated] Full social account management (not just posting)
[extrapolated] Segmented retargeting, up to 5x/day for 30 days

plans.name: Growth
plans.audience: Authors with an established backlist scaling an existing readership, or mounting a larger launch, who want monthly newsletter placement and a bigger review base.
plans.positioning: The top production-and-campaign tier below the fully custom Surge/Orbit engagements — the same full-funnel system as Momentum, scaled up.
plans.outcome: A larger-scale version of the Momentum system: more content, a bigger ARC campaign, more frequent newsletter placement, and expanded retargeting.
services: Segmented retargeting, up to 5x daily for 30 days
deliverables: [extrapolated] Segmented retargeting, up to 5x/day for 30 days

custom_tiers.note: Surge & Orbit — mentioned on pricing page for full catalogue / multi-book / bespoke campaigns.
custom_tiers.pricing_model: custom, dedicated team or custom seat

plan_changes.policy: Upgrading or downgrading is allowed at any time. Current ad spend is taken into account and applied as available credit toward the new plan.

end_of_commitment.policy: On commitment end, everything is handed over via secure transfer if needed — videos created, account info, and related assets. In practice most content is already accessible to the author throughout the engagement, since every content gallery is public to them via their progress-report document/link.

author_involvement.author_provides: A link to the book (or, for a backlist, a link to the author's catalogue), plus optionally any planned discount-deal dates so campaigns can be planned around them.

campaign_management.policy: A dedicated outreach team manages accounts day-to-day, handles ARC/reviewer list outreach, and monitors that campaigns are running smoothly.

genre_support.policy: All genres are supported. Bigger, higher-volume genres tend to see stronger results than smaller genres/subgenres, simply due to reader pool size.

guarantee.name: Atomic Shelf Commitment
guarantee.status: Resolved — reconciles the earlier site/repo copy conflict per your direction.
guarantee.summary: Money-back only for demonstrable non-delivery. Everything else is time-based, and we keep working.
covers: agreed deliverables (videos produced, trailers, listing rewrite, ARC recruitment, preorder setup, retargeting activation)
money_back_trigger_conditions: Zero or near-zero impressions after a full cycle despite content being posted as agreed
Zero or near-zero click-throughs despite measurable impressions
Zero measurable results across the full agreed scope — i.e. the work itself was not fulfilled, not merely underperforming
guarantee.money_back_scope: Refund applies only to the specific line items that were not fulfilled at all — not a blanket refund of the full plan price, and not triggered by results that are simply lower than the estimated range.
does_not_guarantee: A specific rank, ranking, or bestseller position
A specific number of sales, preorders, or downloads
guarantee.time_based_remedy: Outside the zero-delivery trigger, results are treated as a function of time and iteration, not a refund event. If a campaign is underperforming its estimated range, Atomic Shelf continues the agreed work, diagnoses what to adjust, and keeps delivering — it does not refund simply because growth is slower than the estimate.
guarantee.remedy: For confirmed non-delivery: refund of the undelivered portion. For underperformance with delivery confirmed: continued work, diagnosis, and adjustment at no extra cost — not a refund.
guarantee.customer_must: Notify Atomic Shelf within 21 days of the end of the applicable campaign cycle (typically the month-3/90-day mark) to claim a refund under the zero-delivery trigger. Claims outside this window are not eligible for the refund remedy, though underperformance concerns are reviewed under the time-based remedy at any time.
guarantee.terms_url: atomic-shelf-commitment-terms.md (draft — see file; needs legal review before publishing)

review_campaign_disclosure: We can make a book free or provide complimentary copies to selected readers, then invite honest, independent reviews. The free copy is never conditional on posting a review, giving a positive rating, or changing an existing review.
results_disclaimer: Expected ranges are 90-day averages based on 200+ clients over 24 months, measured against each book's pre-campaign baseline — many starting from little to no prior sales. Individual results vary by genre, backlist, and price point.
